key_insight: HTP-Net improves segmentation and counting of dense, slender welding material stubs by preserving boundaries, maintaining topological continuity, and separating overlapping instances.
engineering_relevance: The model supports automated inventory counting and morphological analysis of electrode and wire stubs in welding factories.
method: Wavelet-driven edge preservation retains fine boundaries during downsampling.
Long-range topology modeling reduces disconnections in slender targets.
Orientation-guided segmentation uses rotational priors to reduce excessive non-maximum suppression and overlapping-mask artifacts.
evidence_signal: On custom and public datasets, the abstract reports mAP50 gains of 1.2%–55.3% over existing methods; a factory-deployed system achieved average recognition accuracies of 99% for electrode stubs and 94% for wire stubs.
watch_item: The abstract does not specify dataset sizes, inference speed, or robustness across factory lighting and camera setups, so deployment generalizability needs verification.
paper_title: High-resolution topology-preserving instance segmentation network for vision-based measurement system of dense welding material stubs
